hero.eyebrow: Shared calendars with permissions per entry
hero.title: One calendar for everyone. Different rules for every entry.
hero.lead: Some entries everyone may edit, some are read-only, some only show “Busy” and some stay private – all in the same calendar, and correct in the calendar apps people already use.
hero.note: Free plan forever · Pro features free for {trialDays} days · Hosted in the EU

features.title: Everything a shared calendar should have done from the start
features.lead: Per-entry permissions instead of a separate calendar for every exception.

items.title: Permissions per entry
items.text: Give single entries their own rules for people, groups, roles or share links: edit, read, busy only or hidden. The calendar's defaults cover the rest.

items.title: Groups with roles
items.text: Owner, admin, member and viewer. Members can add their own entries without touching the official ones.

items.title: Your calendar app stays
items.text: Personal feeds for Apple Calendar, Google Calendar, Outlook and Thunderbird. Each entry says whether you may edit it.

items.title: Access you can explain
items.text: Every decision comes with one sentence: “Vic can read this because the board granted read for this entry.”

items.title: Calendars that fill themselves
items.text: Import fixtures and dates from calendar files and event websites on a schedule, with a review queue so nothing lands unseen.

items.title: Private by default
items.text: Hosted in the EU, no ads, no tracking. New calendars start private; export and deletion are one click away.

pricing.title: Simple pricing
pricing.lead: Start free. The owner's plan counts, so one paying organiser covers the whole group.
pricing.seatsHint: Seats are people who create or change entries. People who only read are free (10 per seat).
pricing.trial: Every new account gets the Pro limits for {trialDays} days, then continues on Free unless you upgrade. Nothing is deleted.

pro.name: Pro

limits.eventsWithOverrides: Upcoming entries with their own permissions

items.q: How is this different from sharing a Google or Outlook calendar?
items.a: There you share a whole calendar: everyone sees all details, only free/busy, or may change everything. In {name} every entry can have its own rules, so one calendar replaces the extra calendars you would otherwise create for every exception.

items.q: Do I have to switch calendar apps?
items.a: No. Everyone gets a personal feed for Apple Calendar, Google Calendar, Outlook or Thunderbird that only contains what they may see. Entries say in the app whether you may edit them.

items.q: Is the Free plan really free?
items.a: Yes, without time limit and without a credit card. New accounts get the Pro limits for {trialDays} days on top; afterwards you continue on Free.

items.q: What happens when I downgrade or a limit is reached?
items.a: Nothing is deleted and nothing becomes visible to more people. Anything over the limit is kept read-only, existing permissions stay in force, and only adding more is paused.

items.q: Who has to pay in a group?
items.a: The plan of a calendar's owner counts for everyone in it. If the organiser has Pro, all members get the Pro features in that calendar – with a Free account.
You pay for seats: people who create or change entries. People who only read are free, ten per seat. A club with 200 members and 8 organisers pays for 8 seats.
On servers in the EU. You can export your data and delete your account at any time.

cta.text: Create a calendar, invite your group and subscribe in your calendar app – in a few minutes.

bot.title: {bot}: the {name} importer
bot.lead: Users of {name} can keep calendars up to date with dates from public web pages – fixtures of a league, a school's term dates, a venue's programme. If you found {bot} in your server logs, it fetched a page of your website that a user added as an import source.

what.title: What it fetches
what.text: Only the single pages that users added as import sources, over http or https, no links beyond them. It runs no JavaScript, submits no forms and never logs in. Responses are limited to 3 MB and calendar, HTML and JSON content.

robots.title: robots.txt
robots.text: {bot} respects robots.txt and caches it for up to 24 hours. If your robots.txt disallows a page for {bot} or for all user agents, the import fails with “Website disallows automated access” – users cannot override this.

rate.title: Rate limits
rate.text: At most one request every 10 seconds per domain, across all users. It honours Retry-After and backs off on 429 and 503 responses. Pages are re-checked on the import's schedule – at most hourly, for most sources weekly or daily – with conditional requests (ETag, Last-Modified), so unchanged pages cost you almost nothing.

processing.title: What happens with the content
processing.text: The page's text is turned into calendar entries, partly with the help of a language model, and shown to the user who added the source for review. Event descriptions are stored as plain text with a link back to your page.
